reason: The hypothesis relies on specific claims about CSRO formation via heat treatment and its effects on magnetic exchange, domain wall pinning, and mechanical properties. The cited evidence (E1) discusses a different mechanism (paramagnetic nanoparticles) for reducing coercivity while maintaining strength, and (E2) describes mechanically derived short-range order in a different alloy system, not thermally induced CSRO in FeCoNi-based alloys. Neither passage supports the key premises linking heat-treatment-induced CSRO to the proposed magnetic and mechanical outcomes.
premises: Nanoscale CSRO clusters can be induced by controlled heat treatments in rare-earth-free HEAs.
CSRO clusters moderate the distribution of magnetic exchange energies, creating a uniform local magnetic environment.
A uniform local magnetic environment enables a well-defined, reversible second-order magnetic phase transition at low fields.
CSRO clusters reduce domain wall pinning, thereby lowering hysteresis.
CSRO clusters relieve local stress, maintaining efficient heat exchange and mechanical robustness.
